example_summary: Y Ltd. earns ₹ 10,01,00,000 in A.Y. 2026-27. Since income crosses ₹ 10 crore, marginal relief caps tax liability at ₹ 3,22,00,000, saving ₹ 14,33,600.

### Statutory Tax Rates & Surcharge Matrix for Domestic Companies

| Statutory Criteria | Basic Tax Rate | Surcharge Rate (Income > ₹ 1 Cr to ₹ 10 Cr) | Surcharge Rate (Income > ₹ 10 Cr) | Health & Education Cess |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gross Receipts/Turnover ≤ ₹ 400 Cr** *(in P.Y. 2023-24)* | 25% | 7% | 12% | 4% |
| **Gross Receipts/Turnover > ₹ 400 Cr** *(in P.Y. 2023-24)* | 30% | 7% | 12% | 4% |
| **Concessional Regime u/s 115BAA / 115BAB** | 22% / 15% | Flat 10% | Flat 10% | 4% |


### Statutory Rules for Marginal Relief

* **Applicability Trigger:** Marginal relief applies when Total Income slightly exceeds the threshold limit of ₹ 1 Crore or ₹ 10 Crore.
* **Statutory Restriction:** The tax payable (including surcharge) on Total Income exceeding the threshold limit shall NOT exceed the aggregate of:
  1. Tax payable on the exact threshold limit (₹ 1 Crore or ₹ 10 Crore, including applicable lower surcharge).
  2. The excess amount of Total Income over the threshold limit.
* **Formula for Marginal Relief:**
  $$\text{Marginal Relief} = \text{Tax (incl. Surcharge) on Total Income} - \left[ \text{Tax on Threshold Limit} + (\text{Total Income} - \text{Threshold Limit}) \right]$$


> [!IMPORTANT] Surcharge Transition Spike:
> When Total Income crosses ₹ 10 Crore, surcharge jumps from 7% to 12%. Marginal relief protects the assessee from a disproportionate tax burden where the increase in tax exceeds the increase in total income.
